fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`AcliClient.search_issues` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:398-453`)
memoizes its full result set per JQL string in `self._search_cache` — an unbounded dict with
no TTL and no invalidation anywhere in the class — and it caches negative (empty) answers too.
The docstring scopes the cache to "avoid redundant fetches when the caller paginates", but
nothing enforces that scope: any caller that re-asks the same JQL over time on one client gets
a permanently stale answer. Proven root cause of bug d30c (dutiable-shaded-honeyeater), where
an index-visibility poll re-issued two constant JQLs on one client and only the first attempt
ever reached Jira. The only correct handling in the tree reaches into the private attribute
from outside the class: `access_check.py:176-178` does `cache.pop(jql, None)` before each
retry, and the d30c fix (`tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` `_fresh_search`,
~:393-416) copies that reach-in. The freshness invariant is undocumented, unenforced, and
satisfied only by encapsulation violations.

## Approach

1. **Establish client lifetime and document it at the cache definition.** Evidence already
   read from the tree: `reconcile_helpers.bind_operation_runtime`
   (`reconcile_helpers.py:675`) composes "the ONE operation runtime for this pass" per pass;
   `_backend_registry.select_backend` (`_backend_registry.py:60-76`) constructs a fresh
   backend on every call (no caching); the production entrypoint runs one
   `reconcile.reconcile_once` per process invocation (`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:450`).
   So an `AcliClient` — and its `_search_cache` — lives at most ONE reconcile pass. Record
   this at the cache definition in `acli.py` and in the audit comment on this ticket.
2. **Add the supported freshness door**: an `AcliClient.invalidate_search_cache(jql: str |
   None = None)` method — evicts the one JQL entry when given, clears the whole memo when
   `None`. Chosen over a `fresh=True` kwarg because it is purely additive (no
   `search_issues` signature change on the transport port, `_backend.py`) and matches the
   evict-then-search shape both existing call sites already use. Move `self._search_cache`
   initialization into `AcliClient.__init__` so the method needs no `hasattr` dance (and
   `search_issues` drops its lazy-init branch — a complexity improvement).
3. **Migrate both reach-in sites onto the door**: `access_check.py:176-178` and
   `_fresh_search` in `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` call
   `invalidate_search_cache(jql)` via a callable-guarded lookup (both sites accept arbitrary
   client classes/stubs today, so the guarded lookup preserves that tolerance while using
   the supported name).
4. **Document the negative-caching hazard** in the `search_issues` docstring: negative
   (empty) results are cached; a caller that re-asks the same JQL for freshness must call
   `invalidate_search_cache` first.
5. **Audit `binding_recovery.py:342-346`**: the pending-recovery loop issues each
   `labels = "rebar-id:<local_id>"` JQL once per pending id per pass (the hyphen fallback is
   a distinct JQL string), and its `search_miss_count` corroboration accumulates ACROSS
   passes — where each pass constructs a fresh client (step 1), so repeated misses are
   genuinely fresh queries and `_MISSES_BEFORE_UNBIND` cannot be satisfied by replays of one
   cached answer. Record this proof in the ticket comment and in the cache-definition note.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py` — init cache in `__init__`, add
  `invalidate_search_cache`, document lifetime + negative caching in the docstrings.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py` — migrate the JQL retry loop's
  reach-in onto `invalidate_search_cache`.
- `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` — migrate `_fresh_search` onto
  `invalidate_search_cache`.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_search_cache_freshness.py` — new unit tests for the
  memo + door.

## Testing

Unit tests (new file, subprocess stubbed at the `AcliClient._run` seam, counting invocations):

- Happy: two `search_issues` calls with the same JQL run ONE subprocess (pins the existing
  memo, including a negative first answer staying cached).
- Freshness door: `invalidate_search_cache(jql)` then re-search re-runs the subprocess and
  returns the refreshed answer (a negative-to-positive flip becomes visible — the d30c
  class).
- Full clear: `invalidate_search_cache()` empties the memo for all JQLs.
- Edge: invalidating a never-searched JQL is a no-op (no raise, memo unchanged).

Existing coverage guards the migrations: the access-check retry loop and live-E2E poll tests
keep passing with the reach-in replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `AcliClient` lifetime question is answered (one pass per instance in production)
      and documented at the cache definition in `acli.py` — checked by reading the committed
      docstring/comment citing `bind_operation_runtime` and `select_backend`.
- [ ] `invalidate_search_cache(jql=None)` exists and `access_check.py` plus the d30c E2E
      poll use it instead of popping `_search_cache` directly — checked by
      `grep -rn "_search_cache" src tests` showing no reach-in outside `acli.py`, and by
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_search_cache_freshness.py`.
- [ ] The `search_issues` docstring states that negative results are cached and repeat-query
      callers must invalidate first — checked by reading the docstring.
- [ ] `binding_recovery.py:342-346` is audited: the proof that per-pass client construction
      makes cross-pass miss corroboration fresh is recorded as a comment on this ticket —
      checked by the comment's presence.
